channel.title: Lexus recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Lexus RC, GS and IS fuel pump may quit
item.description: The low-pressure fuel pump that sits inside the fuel tank can stop working. That pump pushes gasoline to the engine, so if it fails the engine can sputter and stall, possibly while you are driving. Toyota has already mailed letters warning owners about the safety risk, and the full repair is still being prepared. Dealers will replace the entire fuel pump assembly at no cost, and a second letter will go out once the remedy is available.

item.title: Lexus NX, RX and TX backup camera may not display
item.description: On certain 2022-2025 Lexus NX350 and NX250, 2023-2026 RX350, and 2024-2026 TX350 vehicles, the backup camera picture may not come up on the screen when you shift into reverse. Without that picture you cannot see what is directly behind the vehicle, which federal rules require. Dealers will update the camera software, or replace the camera if the update does not fix it, free of charge. Owner letters were mailed May 15, 2026.

item.title: Toyota, Lexus and Subaru rearview camera may freeze
item.description: Toyota is recalling certain 2022 through 2026 Toyota and Lexus vehicles and the Subaru Solterra that have the Panoramic View Monitor camera system. Models include RAV4, Highlander, Prius, Sienna Hybrid, Camry Hybrid, Mirai, bZ4X and the Lexus NX and TX Hybrid. A software error can cause the backup camera picture to freeze or go blank when the car is in reverse, so these vehicles do not meet the federal rear visibility standard.

item.title: Lexus NX front headrests can come out too easily
item.description: On some Lexus NX and RX models, the head restraints — the headrests on the driver's and front passenger's seats — can be pulled out without pressing the release button that is supposed to hold them in place. If a headrest comes out and nobody puts it back, the person in that seat has nothing behind their head, and a hit from behind is much more likely to injure their neck. A dealer replaces both front headrests for free.

item.title: Toyota Grand Highlander and Lexus TX curtain airbags deploy wrong
item.description: The side curtain airbags drop down from above the side windows in a crash and are meant to keep people from being thrown out of the vehicle. On these vehicles the airbag may not unroll the way it should, and if a window is open it can partly deploy outside the vehicle instead of covering the window opening. When that happens it does not protect the people sitting beside it as well as it is supposed to.

item.title: Lexus LS front passenger seat sensor may misread occupant
item.description: On these cars with the Executive Package, parts inside the front passenger seat may rub against each other. That can confuse the sensor built into the seat, the one that figures out whether someone is sitting there and how big they are. The airbag system uses that information to decide how to fire the passenger airbag, so in a crash the airbag may not go off the way it should. A dealer will inspect and repair the seat for free.

item.title: Toyota and Lexus front passenger airbag may not inflate
item.description: These Toyota and Lexus vehicles have a sensor in the front passenger seat that tells the airbag system whether someone is sitting there. A short circuit can develop inside that sensor. If it does, the front passenger airbag may not inflate during a crash, so whoever is riding in that seat could be hurt worse than they otherwise would be. The dealer will inspect the sensor and replace it if needed, free of charge. Owner letters are being mailed in stages.

item.title: Toyota and Lexus steering wiring can disable driver's airbag
item.description: Inside the steering column is a coiled ribbon of wiring that keeps the driver's airbag connected as the steering wheel turns. On these vehicles, one electrical connection in that part may not have been welded well enough. If it comes apart, the driver's airbag is switched off and will not inflate in a crash. This recall also means these vehicles do not meet the federal crash-protection standard for occupant safety. Dealers will inspect this part and replace it at no cost if needed.

item.title: Lexus RX350 shipping hook left on, fire risk
item.description: Before a new vehicle is shipped, a metal hook is attached underneath so it can be tied down during transport. On these SUVs, that hook was never taken off before the vehicle was sold. If someone rear-ends the vehicle, the leftover hook can be driven into the fuel filler pipe — the tube that runs from the gas cap down to the tank. Damaging that pipe can let gasoline escape, and spilled fuel can catch fire.

item.title: Toyota and Lexus fuel pumps may fail, stalling engine
item.description: Toyota is recalling a large number of Toyota and Lexus vehicles from the 2017 through 2020 model years, including Camry, Corolla, RAV4, Highlander, Tacoma, Tundra, Sienna and many Lexus models. The low-pressure fuel pump, which sits inside the fuel tank and sends gasoline to the engine, may fail. If it fails, the engine can stall while you are driving. This recall expands an earlier recall covering the same fuel pump problem.

item.title: Toyota and Lexus Vehicles: Fuel Pump Can Stall Engine
item.description: The fuel pump sits inside the gas tank and pushes gas to the engine. On these Toyota and Lexus vehicles, that pump can fail. If it fails, the engine can stall, meaning it shuts off while you are driving. A stall in traffic leaves you without power and can lead to a crash. This recall started in January 2020 and Toyota expanded it twice in March 2020, adding some model years and removing others, so the covered list changed. A dealer replaces the pump at no charge.

item.title: Lexus LS run-flat tires may shed their tread
item.description: Toyota found that on some 2018 Lexus LS sedans with run-flat tires, the way the tires were mounted onto the wheels may have cracked a stiff reinforcing layer inside the tire wall. A cracked layer can let the tread — the rubber that grips the road — peel away from the rest of the tire. If that happens while you are driving, the car can become hard to steer and control.

item.title: Land Cruiser and LX 570 passenger airbags may deactivate
item.description: There is a wire under the front passenger seat that tells the car whether the seat belt is buckled and pulled tight. Over years of use that wire can break. If it does, the car shuts off the front passenger's front airbag, knee airbag, and the side airbag built into that seat. Those airbags would then not inflate in a crash, which matters most for whoever is riding in the front passenger seat. A dealer will fix or replace the seat belt assembly.

item.title: Toyota and Lexus SUVs have wrong weight-limit labels
item.description: These trucks and SUVs left the factory with an incorrect sticker showing how much weight the vehicle can safely carry. The label itself does not break anything, but if you trust the wrong number you could put in too many people, too much cargo, or too heavy a load. An overloaded vehicle is harder to steer and stop and puts extra strain on the tires, which raises the chance of a crash. Toyota is mailing owners corrected labels free of charge.
